questions.question: State the Arrhenius and Brønsted-Lowry definitions of acids and bases, and use the behaviour of ammonia in water to show why the Brønsted-Lowry definitions are the stronger pair.
questions.expected_answer: Arrhenius: an acid releases hydrogen ions (H⁺) in water and a base releases hydroxide ions (OH⁻). Brønsted-Lowry: an acid is a proton donor and a base is a proton acceptor. Ammonia breaks the Arrhenius scheme because NH₃ contains no hydroxide yet gives a basic solution. The equation NH₃ + H₂O ⇌ NH₄⁺ + OH⁻ shows ammonia accepting a proton from water to form ammonium, while the water that donated becomes hydroxide. Under Brønsted-Lowry, ammonia is a base simply because it accepts a proton — the hydroxide in the solution is generated from water during the transfer rather than supplied by ammonia's formula. Arrhenius also restricts acid-base chemistry to water as solvent, another limitation Brønsted-Lowry removes.

questions.question: Define a conjugate acid-base pair and identify both pairs in HNO₃ + H₂O → H₃O⁺ + NO₃⁻. Then write the two equations that prove the hydrogen carbonate ion HCO₃⁻ is an ampholyte.
questions.expected_answer: A conjugate acid-base pair is two species that differ by exactly one proton; the member with the extra proton is the acid. In HNO₃ + H₂O → H₃O⁺ + NO₃⁻: pair one is HNO₃ (acid) and NO₃⁻ (conjugate base), since HNO₃ donated a proton to become nitrate; pair two is H₃O⁺ (acid) and H₂O (conjugate base), since water accepted a proton to become hydronium. The pairs link diagonally across the arrow — the two reactants are never a pair, and species two protons apart (like H₂CO₃ and CO₃²⁻) are not conjugates. HCO₃⁻ as an ampholyte: as an acid (donor), HCO₃⁻ + H₂O ⇌ CO₃²⁻ + H₃O⁺; as a base (acceptor), HCO₃⁻ + H₂O ⇌ H₂CO₃ + OH⁻. Donating in one reaction and accepting in another makes it amphiprotic.

questions.question: Write balanced equations for nitric acid reacting with potassium hydroxide, with calcium oxide, and with potassium carbonate, naming the products of each. Then give the colours of bromothymol blue and phenolphthalein in acidic, neutral (where applicable) and basic solutions.
questions.expected_answer: With a metal hydroxide: HNO₃ + KOH → KNO₃ + H₂O — potassium nitrate and water. With a metal oxide: 2HNO₃ + CaO → Ca(NO₃)₂ + H₂O — calcium nitrate and water. With a metal carbonate: 2HNO₃ + K₂CO₃ → 2KNO₃ + H₂O + CO₂ — potassium nitrate, water and carbon dioxide; only the carbonate reaction fizzes, and the gas is carbon dioxide. All three follow the master pattern acid + base → salt + water, with carbonates adding CO₂ as a third product. Bromothymol blue: yellow in acid, green in neutral solution, blue in base — the only required indicator with a distinct neutral colour. Phenolphthalein: colourless in acid, pink in base, and it stays colourless at neutral.
